items.title: Traders Are Piling Into Taiwan Dollar Options to Bet on Rebound
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Currency traders are stepping up bullish options bets on the Taiwan dollar, signaling a shift in sentiment after the currency suffered its worst July since 2015.</article>

items.title: SEC Alleges Fund Adviser Misled Investors in Pre-IPO Schemes
items.author: Nicola M White
items.content: <article>Investment adviser Adit Ventures and co-founder Eric Munson were accused by the US Securities and Exchange Commission of making false claims about investments and overcharging clients with millions of dollars in undisclosed fees to buy shares of companies including SpaceX and Klarna before they were offered to the public.</article>

items.title: Oil Holds Gains, Yen in Focus After Weakening: Markets Wrap
items.author: Anand Krishnamoorthy and Rob Verdonck
items.content: <article>Oil held onto gains as fading hopes for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz revived inflation concerns before key US data this week.</article>

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 11
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Oil held a three-day gain after President Donald Trump made sweeping new demands on Iran, clouding the outlook for a deal to reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz.</article>

items.title: 777 Partners Files Bankruptcy After Creditors’ Liquidation Push
items.author: Jonathan Randles
items.content: <article>Alternative investment firm 777 Partners has filed for bankruptcy weeks after creditors sought to liquidate what’s left of the company that began unloading its assets more than a year ago.</article>

items.title: Outsiders Pay $6,500 for Help With Sorority Rush
items.content: <article>The push by young women to gain acceptance into sororities at large schools in the Deep South has led to an increase in demand for rush coaches. Bloomberg News Reporter Gabriel Baumgaertner discusses his recent story about the high price tag some parents are willing to invest to help their kids get into the sorority of their dreams. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Touts $3B in Mineral Project to Counter China
items.content: <article>During a recent meeting with top industry executives, the US President announced $3 billion in investments aimed at strengthening the domestic critical minerals and mining sector. The initiative seeks to reduce reliance on supply chains dominated by China. Gary Evans, Chairman and CEO of US Antimony, participated in the discussion and spoke to Bloomberg News about how much he is willing to see the government invest in his firm. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Hims & Hers Lowers Profit Forecast, Shares Drop
items.content: <article>Hims & Hers Health shares are down after the telehealth firm reduced the top end of its adjusted Ebitda forecast for the full year. Madison Muller reports on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Chicago Taps Fitch Senior Director as New CFO Amid Rash of Exits
items.author: Shruti Date Singh
items.content: <article>Chicago is hiring Ashlee Gabrysch, a senior director at Fitch Ratings, as its next chief financial officer, according to a person familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: AI Stock Heavy ETF Risks Spread to Broader Equity Market
items.author: Jin Wu, Denitsa Tsekova and Denise Lu
items.content: A growing share of equity leverage is riding on the same AI names, many of which have seen historic swings.

items.title: Gotham Greens CEO: Not Good To Have an Outbreak Like This
items.content: <article>Craig Stevenson, CEO of Gotham Greens, addressed the ongoing concerns over food safety amid recent recalls linked to salmonella in jalapenos and the widespread Cyclospora outbreak affecting thousands in the U.S. He noted a temporary decline in consumer demand for greens as news of outbreaks circulates, but emphasized that consumer interest in salads remains strong. He speaks with David Gura & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: ETFs Look Safer After Bitcoin Hack, Small Caps | ETF IQ 8/10/2026
items.content: <article>"Bloomberg ETF IQ" focuses on the opportunities, risks and current trends tied to the trillions of dollars in the global exchange traded funds industry. Today's guests: JPMorgan Investment Management Chief ETF Strategist Jon Maier, BlackRock Head of Digital Assets Robert Mitchnick, Avantis Investors CIO Eduardo Repetto, and Raymond James Vice President of ETF Strategy Mayuranki De. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Oil Jumps as Markets Await Middle East Clarity | Closing Bell
items.content: <article>Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with David Gura, Isabelle Lee, Norah Mulinda and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Hoenig: Upcoming Data Will Be Deciding Factor for Fed
items.content: <article>Thomas Hoenig, Distinguished Senior Fellow at the Mercatus Center, discussed the Federal Reserve's current stance amid recent economic data. He emphasized that the Fed is maintaining a cautious, wait-and-see attitude as it awaits upcoming inflation reports, including CPI and PPI data, which will be critical for shaping future policy decisions. He speaks with David Gura & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Gautam Adani Wins Dismissal of US Securities Fraud Charges
items.author: Patricia Hurtado and David Voreacos
items.content: <article>Gautam Adani won dismissal of US securities fraud charges, ending a blockbuster case that threatened the expansion of the Indian billionaire’s giant conglomerate.</article>

items.title: JBS Returns Leadership to Batista Clan as Scion Named CEO
items.author: Dayanne Sousa
items.content: <article>The world’s largest meat supplier, JBS NV, will be led once again by a member of Brazil’s Batista family, a pivotal move for a global food powerhouse that’s increasingly focused on the US.</article>

items.title: US Stocks End Mixed as Chipmaker Earnings, CPI Due to Set Pace
items.author: Norah Rami and Elena Eisenstadt
items.content: <article>US stocks held steady through Monday’s market close after a strong earnings week as investors continue to navigate the uncertain path of interest rates and war in Iran. The market is gearing up for the final stretch of corporate earnings, with chipmakers set to provide confirmation for the long-winded debate over valuations.</article>

items.title: Emerging Currencies Weaken as US-Iran Standoff Lifts Dollar
items.author: Benjamin Liu, Andras Gergely and Beatriz Amat
items.content: <article>Most emerging-market currencies weakened against the dollar on Monday as fading hopes of an imminent US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz sent Brent futures prices higher.</article>

items.title: Yen Erases Half of Intervention Gains as Traders Test Bessent
items.author: Anya Andrianova and John Cheng
items.content: <article>The yen swung to a loss, sapping momentum from efforts by the US and Japan authorities to boost the currency.</article>

items.title: Gold Nears $4,400 as Traders Weigh Hormuz Standoff, Inflation
items.author: Yvonne Yue Li
items.content: <article>Gold rose to nearly $4,400 an ounce as traders assessed the latest development around the Strait of Hormuz while awaiting the release of a key US inflation report later this week.</article>
